news.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are available through the API
news.summary: OpenAI documents the new Astra and Sol API identifiers, reasoning controls and standard token prices.
news.whyItMatters: The catalog can distinguish a balanced Sol route from the more expensive Astra route using published rates.
news.suggestedAction: Evaluate both on a small set of sanitized tasks before changing team defaults.

news.title: OpenAI adds healthcare model configurations to the Responses API
news.summary: OpenAI made healthcare-specific model configurations available to API organizations through the Responses API. One documented model ID is `gpt-6.2-astra-healthcare`. With web search enabled, the configurations can query a dedicated healthcare index and cite sources when summarizing medical evidence. An API organization can use them without a ChatGPT for Healthcare workspace.
news.whyItMatters: Teams building tools for healthcare clients can evaluate a dedicated evidence search option in their existing Responses API integration.
news.suggestedAction: Test citation coverage on public literature and confirm account and tool eligibility before using protected health information.

news.title: Microsoft warns about malicious Agent Framework Python releases
news.summary: Microsoft’s November 25 update confirms that unauthorized versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of the agent-framework Python meta-package contained credential-stealing code. The releases were uploaded on November 17 and removed from PyPI. Microsoft says its repository remains temporarily unavailable while it investigates, with no confirmed restoration timeline.
news.whyItMatters: Agent development environments and CI builds that installed either release may have exposed credentials.
news.suggestedAction: Check lockfiles, build logs, images and package caches for the affected versions. If present, follow Microsoft’s guidance to rotate accessible credentials, rebuild clean environments and review audit logs.

news.title: Copilot code review billing defaults change on December 30
news.summary: GitHub announced that unset billing policies for code reviews by licensed Copilot members will default to the repository’s organization on December 30, 2026. The change covers Copilot Business and Enterprise. Existing explicit choices persist. Accounts without AI Credits paid usage, with a billing lock, or without a billable customer will use Member billing.
news.whyItMatters: Administrators may need to choose who pays for automated reviews before organizational spending increases.
news.suggestedAction: Review the enterprise or organization Copilot policy and select Member before December 30 if reviews should continue using members’ entitlements.

news.title: Qwen4-Max-Preview retires and routes to Qwen4-Max
news.summary: Alibaba’s Model Studio release log now states that Qwen4-Max-Preview retired on November 25, 2026. Requests using the original preview model ID automatically route to Qwen4-Max and are billed at its standard rate. The preview’s limited-time discount has ended. This changes the backend and billing of callers that retain the preview identifier.
news.whyItMatters: Existing integrations can continue sending requests while their model configuration and costs change.
news.suggestedAction: Find preview model IDs in application configuration, migrate to an explicit supported Qwen4-Max identifier, and check current regional rates and usage bills.

news.title: Cloudflare launches Search for Agents in beta
news.summary: Cloudflare launched Search for Agents in beta across all plans. Enabling it for an onboarded domain creates an AI Search instance, indexes site content and exposes a discoverable /.well-known/search endpoint. Agents retrieve relevant Markdown using GET or HTTP QUERY requests. Ingestion, storage and queries follow AI Search pricing and plan limits.
news.whyItMatters: Teams maintaining customer documentation can offer agent-accessible retrieval through an existing Cloudflare domain.
news.suggestedAction: Pilot it on public documentation, review indexing scope and WAF controls, and check AI Search usage limits before enabling it for a customer domain.

news.title: Alibaba expands decision-model to Frankfurt, Beijing and Tokyo
news.summary: Alibaba’s November 26 release log extends decision-model to Frankfurt, Beijing and Tokyo, following its November 25 Singapore launch. The API handles classification, binary decisions and scoring using text and images. The model page lists input pricing of $0.042 per million tokens in each of those regions and a 268,288-token context window.
news.whyItMatters: Teams evaluating ticket classification or agent routing now have an additional European hosting region to assess.
news.suggestedAction: Check regional endpoint availability and data-handling terms, then evaluate routing accuracy and confidence calibration on representative approved tickets.

news.title: Google adds an agentic upgrade check to Managed Airflow
news.summary: Google’s November 26 release notes introduce an agentic upgrade check for Managed Airflow. After selecting a target version in the Google Cloud console, operators can ask Managed Airflow Agent to inspect environment configuration, DAG source and supporting files. The check produces a compatibility assessment and validation steps through static inspection.
news.whyItMatters: Cloud operations teams can use the assessment to plan DAG changes before an environment upgrade.
news.suggestedAction: Confirm the required agent permissions, select a target environment version and run Upgrade check, then validate its recommendations in a test environment.
